I could not persist the dossier or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`: the workspace is read-only, and shell/file-edit attempts were rejected. I therefore cannot honestly claim the run was completed in the repository.

I did perform a bounded continuation search and recovered the following handoff evidence:

- **1B:** Freedom House documents Biden’s valid 2020 election, continued election-interference prosecutions, Alabama redistricting litigation, and ongoing voter-access disparities. Contrary evidence includes polarization, election distrust, and congressional obstruction. [Freedom House 2024 US report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2024); [DOJ voting-rights statement](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/attorney-general-merrick-b-garland-statement-regarding-58th-anniversary-voting-rights-act).

- **2B:** The Biden administration’s anti-corruption strategy and sanctions architecture continued in 2023; DOJ and independent inspectors-general mechanisms supplied formal oversight. Contrary evidence includes the Menendez bribery case, Supreme Court ethics controversies, and the Biden-family impeachment inquiry, which Freedom House reports produced no credible evidence of criminal wrongdoing by Biden. [Federal Register anti-corruption notice](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2023-27630.pdf); [Freedom House 2024 US report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2024); [Oversight.gov](https://www.oversight.gov/about/inspectors-general).

- **3B:** Real GDP grew 2.5% in 2023 and unemployment was 3.7% in December; administration programs under the IRA and CHIPS Act had documented implementation outputs. Contrary evidence: GAO reports mixed federal progress in evidence-based management and inflation remained a major public concern. [BEA 2023 GDP release](https://www.bea.gov/news/2024/gross-domestic-product-fourth-quarter-and-year-2023-advance-estimate); [BLS 2023 employment release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01052024.htm); [GAO-23-105460](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-105460).

- **4B:** The 2023 National Plan to End Gender-Based Violence documents federal implementation responsibilities, firearms restrictions, VAWA funding, and domestic-violence intervention infrastructure. Contrary evidence: Freedom House still characterizes rape and intimate-partner violence as serious national problems, with state-level variation. [National Plan to End Gender-Based Violence](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/National-Plan-to-End-GBV.pdf); [Freedom House 2024 US report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/united-states/freedom-world/2024).

- **5B:** FBI estimates show violent crime decreased 3% in 2023; Biden formally authorized substantial Ukraine assistance and sought further security and humanitarian funding. Contrary evidence: the Gaza war generated severe civilian-harm and humanitarian concerns, limiting any simple peace-effectiveness interpretation. [FBI 2023 crime statistics](https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases/fbi-releases-2023-crime-in-the-nation-statistics); [State Department Ukraine package](https://2021-2025.state.gov/biden-administration-announces-additional-u-s-military-assistance-for-ukraine-2/); [White House supplemental request](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2023/12/06/statement-from-national-security-advisor-jake-sullivan-on-president-bidens-national-security-supplemental-request/).

- **6B:** Biden’s administration extended New START, maintained a stated arms-control/nonproliferation strategy, and publicly committed to preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon. Contrary evidence: Russia’s war and suspension of treaty cooperation undermined the external security environment. [State Department nuclear-policy briefing](https://2021-2025.state.gov/remarks-at-the-high-level-briefing-on-u-s-nuclear-policy-at-the-tenth-review-conference-on-the-treaty-on-the-non-proliferation-of-nuclear-weapons/); [State Department March 2023 briefing](https://2021-2025.state.gov/briefings/department-press-briefing-march-1-2023/).

- **7B:** The administration’s 2023 foreign-policy record includes Ukraine coalition-building, Israel support, humanitarian assistance, and stated commitment to a two-state outcome. Contrary evidence includes the gap between humanitarian warnings and limited leverage over Israeli conduct in Gaza. [State Department G7 statement](https://2021-2025.state.gov/g7-foreign-ministers-meeting-statement/); [GovInfo October 19 address](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/DCPD-202300917).

- **8B:** Biden exercised formal executive authority through the East Palestine response order, federal management agenda, economic legislation, and security appropriations. Contrary evidence: GAO found incomplete goals and inconsistent quarterly reporting, indicating uneven administrative effectiveness. [Executive Order 14108](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2023/09/26/2023-21174.html); [GAO-23-106354](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-106354); [White House 2023 agenda memo](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/LaBolt-Memo_Biden-Harris-Agenda-Delivered-in-2023.pdf).
